newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TASS plans to double Russia long distance capacity.
newsitem.headline: TASS plans to double Russia long distance capacity.

text.p: Russian news agency ITAR-TASS and U.S. Transworld Communications Inc have launched a long-distance telephone network which will begin operation this year and plans to double public network capacity, Transworld said on Friday.
The network has a licence to work with the main domestic Public Switched Telephone Network and will work in cooperation with domestic long distance companies, officials said.
Andrei Grigoriyev, chief executive of the company, called TASS-Loutch Telecom, told Reuters sales would be in the billions of dollars.

Transworld's Advanced Communications Technologies (ACT) subsidiary and TASS's Tass-Telecom subsidiary each have 50 percent stakes in the deal, he said. Privately held Transworld Communications is based in McLean, Virginia.

ACT chief executive Mikhail Alexeyev said planned network capacity after five years with two Loutch-2 Russian-built communications satellites and 50 ground stations would be 2.8 billion minutes per year.
"Two point eight billion minutes would be $1.5 billion per year at existing tariffs," he said.
He said the PSTN network, operating near capacity, carried about 3.3 billion minutes per year.
The two satellites would account for about 75 percent of current Russian commercial telecoms capacity, he said.
One satellite and about six earth stations will begin operations later this year, covering European Russia and Siberia as far east as Irkutsk.

Alexeyev declined to say how much the company was investing in the project but said earth stations, including licences, would cost about $2.5 million. An industry source estimated the Loutch-2 telecom satellite cost $180-$250 million each.
"We phase in the network as we establish the cash flow," he said. "We fund the first six or seven earth stations and then will have enough cash to fund the following," he said.

One satellite is already in orbit and a second focusing on European Russia and planned for launch in mid-1998 is almost built, he said. A third satellite covering eastern Russia is tentatively planned for 1999 launch.
The company will install 43 more nine-metre dishes over a year and a half period from spring 1998, a company statement said.

Alexeyev said TASS-Loutch was the only company with a licence to work as part of the public PSTN network and would seek to complement long-distance operator Rostelekom rather than compete directly with it in major markets.
"You want to play the ministry strategy, otherwise there is no way to enter the game," he said.
TASS, one of Russia's two largest news agencies, also has a telecommunications service and is one of three Intelsat satellite communications resellers in Russia, Alexeyev said.
The project is developed under the Russian governments People's Telephone programme, which aims to build up domestic long-distance telephone links.
